result.title: Geometric Relevance Is Not Sufficient: Evaluating Focused Post-Training Supervision in Diffusion Docking
result.comment: 17 pages, 5 figures; accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 AI4DD Workshop
result.summary: Diffusion-based molecular docking requires learning a corrective score field across a broad corruption distribution, yet individual pose errors can differ substantially in their structural consequences. This creates a post-training conflict between preserving broad score-field coverage and concentrating supervision on corrections that appear more relevant to docking geometry. Using DiffDock, a fixed-budget study compares broad continuation with torsional supervision focused on Cartesian consequence or conditional target consistency, and with a broad/focused mixture. Evaluation separates fixed score fidelity, generated-pose quality, best-of-10 sampling capacity, and confidence-selected Top-1 docking performance. At <5 Angstrom, broad continuation had the highest mean Top-1 success among trained policies, and focused or mixed supervision showed no consistent advantage under the tested budget. The starting model had better fixed score fidelity, whereas the evaluated broad-continuation model had higher mean Top-1 success with the same aggregate best-of-10 recovery. Focusing supervision on structurally consequential or more consistently specified corrections did not consistently improve returned-pose success over broad continuation.

AI.brief_summary: 该文在 DiffDock 上做固定预算的后训练对比：宽泛继续训练、按 Cartesian 后果或条件目标一致性聚焦扭转监督，以及宽泛与聚焦混合；并从分数保真度、生成位姿质量、best-of-10 采样能力与置信度选择 Top-1 四个层面分别评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 「聚焦看似更相关的监督反而无稳定收益」与对保真度、采样容量、选择成功率的分离评估，可能为 latent 推理中轨迹监督是否应集中到关键步骤、以及区分内部表示保真与答案成功率提供核查线索，但分子对接领域相距较远，迁移性需人工判断。
